value.title: Tally columns
value.complexity_breakdown: S=1 I=1 D=2 N=1 F=0 T=1 → 6 → CS-3. Data/State scores 2: the feature stores derived values in committed documents, which is the whole hazard.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Tally columns give a dd table spreadsheet-style sums with nothing implicit: a column is marked `in` before it participates, marked columns sum into a footer row, a column marked `total` holds each row's sum, and the grand total is the footer cell of the total column — the intersection of the two axes. The tally is WRITTEN INTO the .dd.json rather than derived at render, because agents read these numbers with `jq` instead of summing rows themselves; a number that is not in the JSON cannot be queried at all. Storing it creates a failure mode nothing else in the repo can see, so `dd validate` recomputes and compares. This plan is RETROACTIVE: the substrate is already built, committed and independently reviewed APPROVE; what remains is documentation, three minor review findings, and two bodies of work each gated on a ruling that is with Jordan.

value.claim: An agent reading only `dd docs get how-to-add-a-schema` can declare a tally column correctly on the first attempt — the page names `tally`, its two values, and the numeric-type restriction.
The shipped docs state what a stored tally is, why `dd validate` recomputes it, and that a hand-edited tally passes `dd build --check` — the exact case a reader would otherwise trust.
`dd build --check` reports no drift on the regenerated docs corpus, and `check-dd-docs` passes — the docs pipeline stayed the source of truth.
A table whose FIRST column is tally-marked renders a labelled footer row, not an unlabelled one.
The empty-row semantic (a row with no addend values stores `0`, not absent) is stated in the docs rather than left as a silent choice.
A stored tally that is a non-number is reported with the same clarity as one that is merely wrong — the parse-vs-E463 asymmetry is documented in the manifest note.
The stored tally cannot silently disagree with its rows: a planted mismatch is named by `dd validate` with its location and both numbers, and a writer verb repairs it.
value.note: Already true and proven in the substrate phase — planted live, E463 x2 exit 1, repaired by an unrelated `dd add`. Carried here so the plan's acceptance covers the invariant, not just the new work.

value.title: Docs and review polish
value.brief: The measured gap: `tally` appears in ZERO of the four baked chapters, and `how-to-add-a-schema` teaches `gate_terminal` by name while never mentioning `tally` — so an agent following the docs cannot find the feature. Docs are GENERATED (`docs/how/dd/*.md` + `dd-docs-manifest.json` -> `docs-content.ts`, drift-guarded by `check-dd-docs`), so this edits source markdown and regenerates; hand-editing the emitted module fails the gate. Folded in here because two of the three review findings are themselves documentation — the empty-row `0` semantic and the parse-vs-E463 asymmetry are sentences, not code — and only the footer-label fix is a code change.
value.objective: Make the feature discoverable from the shipped documentation, and close the three minor findings the review recorded rather than fixed.
delivers: `tally` taught in how-to-add-a-schema §2 + Checklist, beside gate_terminal
footer label fix when column 0 is marked
value.key_risks: Nothing fails when docs omit a feature — there is no gate for discoverability, so the only detector is a human reading the chapter. The acceptance criteria are written as reader outcomes for that reason.

value.title: Schema editing verbs
value.brief: GATED on Jordan's Q1 ruling — write vs print — and not to be designed further before it. Workshop 001 has the surface at Contract Ready: verb roster, grammar, refusal matrix, the winning-rung rule, and the doctor-backed impact check. The reason this is a gate and not a task: `dd schema` is read-only today and `src/acts/schema.ts` contains no filesystem write, so dd has NEVER written a schema. Every document-side safety property — staging, atomic rename, rollback, sibling lockstep, validate-before-write — has no schema analogue and would have to be built or declined deliberately; the blast radius spans every document resolving to the schema; and the four-rung ladder makes 'which file do I write' ambiguous enough that a write verb could manufacture the shadowing dd already reports as degraded. A zero-write alternative (print the fragment for the agent to apply) satisfies the original ask with no new write surface and is scored but unruled.
value.objective: Give agents first-class tooling to declare and mark schema columns instead of hand-editing JSON against a silently lossy allow-list.
delivers: (pending Q1) the verb set specified in workshop 001, or the print-only alternative
value.key_risks: Q1 UNRULED — Jordan's. Implementation must not start before it. Choosing wrong is a capability-class mistake, not a refactor, because it is the moment dd stops being a schema reader.
value.note: Blocked on Jordan's Q1 ruling (write vs print). Not to be designed further before it — the o-prime holds this pending the capability-class finding that dd has never written a schema.

value.title: Float precision policy
value.brief: GATED on Jordan's Q2 ruling. The seam is already in place and isolated: every sum in the feature leaves through `roundToDataPrecision` (`src/core/tally.ts:81`), which today rounds to the precision the column's own data carries, returns integers untouched, and refuses to invent precision beyond 15 places. Kept as its own phase — not folded into the docs phase — precisely because it is gated on a DIFFERENT ruling; bundling gated work with ungated work is how a whole phase ends up blocked on someone else's decision. If Jordan confirms the current policy the phase closes with a docs line and no code change.
value.objective: Rule and lock the precision at which sums are stored.
delivers: (pending Q2) confirmed or replaced policy inside one function body, plus the stated semantic in the docs
value.key_risks: Q2 UNRULED — Jordan's. The seam (`roundToDataPrecision`, src/core/tally.ts:81) keeps the cost at one function body while nothing stores a tally. The risk is not the ruling being late; it is the ruling being late RELATIVE TO ADOPTION. Whoever adds the first tally mark to a real schema should check this row first.
value.note: Blocked on Jordan's Q2 ruling (float precision policy). THE TRIGGER IS ADOPTION, NOT MERGE — measured 2026-08-12, before the merge: zero schemas in this repo mark a tally (`grep -rl '"tally"' .dd/schemas/` → none) and zero committed .dd.json carries a stored tally, so the blast radius of a late ruling is currently ZERO — it changes one function body and the tests that pin it, and rewrites no bytes. That stops being true the day the FIRST repo schema adopts a tally mark: from then on the policy decides values already committed to documents, and a reversal is a corpus rewrite rather than a code edit. So the real constraint is: Q2 must be ruled BEFORE any repo schema adopts a tally mark — which is a docs/adoption event, not a merge event.
